title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-11-02
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v8.01 Professional -> FLAC
source: Disc 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) DDisc 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a legendary late‑'69 set highlighted by an epic Dark Star that flows into St. Stephen, The Eleven and Death Don't Have No Mercy.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered soundboard is crystal‑clear—often called the best 1969 recording on Archive—with superb bass definition and no audible flaws. Musically the show is a tour‑de‑force: a 30‑minute Dark Star that erupts into a Feelin’ Groovy/Tighten‑Up jam, then rolls straight into St. Stephen, The Eleven and a heart‑wrenching Death Don't Have No Mercy. Reviewers rave about the seamless segues, Jerry’s soaring guitar tone and vocal punch, and the overall high‑octane flow of the evening.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 15 detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both performance and audio; recording is described as pristine and the musical setlist is repeatedly called exceptional.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear remaster by Charlie Miller; praised as best‑ever 1969 sound with superb bass clarity and no noticeable dropouts or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑energy late‑’69 set with seamless segues; the Dark Star/Feelin' Groovy/Tighten‑Up jam chain leads into St. Stephen, The Eleven and Death Don't Have No Mercy, creating a climax that reviewers call one of the era’s finest.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is described as powerful, muscular and soaring; his vocal on the final line of St. Stephen is highlighted as uniquely intense.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass clarity is specifically praised as “the BEST ever BASS clarity,” indicating a strong Phil Lesh performance.
